Algebra 2 | Quarter 2 | Unit 3: Linear Systems and Matrices

Where Does the Rider Land?

Solving a jump and a landing ramp together

Duration
55 minutes
Grade level
Grades 10–11
Topic
Systems of Equations
Standards
HSA-REI.C.6, HSA-REI.C.7, HSA-REI.D.12

Students solve systems of two equations by graphing, substitution and elimination, solve linear–quadratic systems (a jump’s path meeting a landing ramp), and graph systems of inequalities.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Solve a system of two linear equations by substitution or elimination and interpret the solution.
  • Solve a linear–quadratic system algebraically and check it with a graph.
  • Decide which solutions make sense in context.
  • Graph a system of linear inequalities and identify the feasible region.

3Essential question

How can two equations, a rider’s path and a ramp’s surface, tell you exactly where the rider lands?

5MTB connection

A jump’s flight path is (approximately) a parabola, and a landing ramp is (approximately) a line. Where they meet is where the rider touches down: the solution of a linear–quadratic system.

Solving systems also answers race questions (when does a faster rider catch a slower one?) and planning questions (which combinations of laps and rest fit in a training session?).

The mathOn the trail
Linear–quadratic systemFlight path and landing ramp
IntersectionTouchdown point
Solution outside the domainWhere the ramp would be if it were longer

7MTB activity

MTB Problem-Based Exercise

Design the Landing

Use linear–quadratic systems to test whether a rider lands on each proposed landing ramp.

You’ll need: Graphing calculator or graphing app (to check); Graph paper

The full lesson plan is for teachers

Teachers also get the mathematical foundation with worked examples, a 5-stage teaching plan with timings, step-by-step activity instructions, 4 guided examples with solutions, 9 practice problems, a 4-question exit ticket, a printable worksheet, common misconceptions, differentiation ideas and the complete answer key.
